title: Simplicial homotopy equivalences are realization weak equivalences
statement: Use small simplicial sets, geometric realization and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $u:A\to B$ and $v:B\to A$ be simplicial maps. Suppose there are simplicial maps $H:A\times\Delta^1\to A$ and $J:B\times\Delta^1\to B$ whose endpoint restrictions are $vu,\mathrm{id}_A$ and $uv,\mathrm{id}_B$, respectively, in either order for each pair. Then $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: its realization induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups at every basepoint of $|A|$. No Kan or nonemptiness assumption on $A$ or $B$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13 (Kerodon 00UB), forward implication; Construction 3.6.5.1 (Kerodon 0148, https://kerodon.net/tag/0148) identifies a simplicial cylinder homotopy with a continuous homotopy after realization, without Kan assumptions. Either endpoint orientation is allowed by reversing the continuous interval. Remark 3.1.7.6 is a mapping-set characterization, not the realization reference. Online sources read; archival copies WANTED.

proof.text:
We first construct the realization of an arbitrary cylinder homotopy $h:K\times\Delta^1\to L$, with endpoint maps $h_0,h_1:K\to L$, using the quotient realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $a\in K_n$ and $\lambda=(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_n)\in|\Delta^n|$, put $S_i=\sum_{j=i}^n\lambda_j$ and $S_{n+1}=0$. The closed regions $R_i=\{(\lambda,t):S_{i+1}\leq t\leq S_i\}$ cover $|\Delta^n|\times[0,1]$. Let $r_i:[n+1]\to[n]$ repeat $i$, and let $e_i:[n+1]\to[1]$ take indices $0,\ldots,i$ to $0$ and indices $i+1,\ldots,n+1$ to $1$. On $R_i$ use the point of $|L|$ represented by the $(n+1)$-simplex $h(K(r_i)a,e_i)$ and weights
$$(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{i-1},S_i-t,t-S_{i+1},\lambda_{i+1},\ldots,\lambda_n).$$
All weights are nonnegative and their sum is one. For fixed $a,i$ they depend continuously on $(\lambda,t)$, so the characteristic map of this simplex gives a continuous map on $R_i$.

source.place: Construction 3.6.5.1 (0148), for a 1-simplex in Fun(K,L); explicit agent prism expansion of the continuous realization homotopy. Corollary 3.6.2.2 (013E) supplies the source's finite-factor product identification; the argument below constructs the homotopy directly instead.

proof.text:
At an adjacent seam $t=S_i$, the formula on $R_{i-1}$ assigns weight zero to the copy of $(i-1,1)$, and the formula on $R_i$ assigns weight zero to the copy of $(i,0)$. After deleting these zero-weight vertices both formulas use the same ordered list
$$(0,0),\ldots,(i-1,0),(i,1),\ldots,(n,1)$$
in $[n]\times[1]$, with weights $(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_n)$. Their images agree because $h$ commutes with face maps. Nonadjacent overlaps have the intervening $\lambda_j=0$, and repeated deletion gives the same equality. Thus the formulas agree on all intersections. They paste continuously on the prism: the inverse image of a closed subset of $|L|$ is a finite union of subsets closed in the closed $R_i$, hence closed in the prism. This uses exactly the face identifications and characteristic maps specified in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Construction 3.6.5.1 (0148), for a 1-simplex in Fun(K,L); explicit agent prism expansion of the continuous realization homotopy. Corollary 3.6.2.2 (013E) supplies the source's finite-factor product identification; the argument below constructs the homotopy directly instead.

proof.text: The prism formulas respect every realization relation in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a face, insert a zero coordinate at the omitted vertex. If the cut is at that vertex, both split weights are zero; otherwise the omitted weight is zero at its one level. Deleting these entries gives exactly the lower-dimensional formula. For a degeneracy, two consecutive coordinates $\lambda_j,\lambda_{j+1}$ correspond to a repeated vertex of $a$. If the cut is outside that pair, both entries are at the same level in $[1]$ and the realization relation adds their weights. If the cut is inside the pair, write $T=\sum_{k>j+1}\lambda_k$. The total weight of this repeated vertex at level $1$ is $\min(\lambda_j+\lambda_{j+1},\max(0,t-T))$, and its level-$0$ weight is the complementary weight. These are precisely the split weights for the merged coordinate $\lambda_j+\lambda_{j+1}$; each consecutive repetition at a fixed level is removed by a degeneracy relation. The cumulative sums away from the pair are unchanged. Hence both cases give the formula for the un-repeated simplex. Every monotone map factors as a surjection followed by an injection, so faces and degeneracies check all relations. The prism maps therefore define a function $\widetilde h:|K|\times[0,1]\to|L|$.

source.place: Construction 3.6.5.1 (0148), for a 1-simplex in Fun(K,L); explicit agent prism expansion of the continuous realization homotopy. Corollary 3.6.2.2 (013E) supplies the source's finite-factor product identification; the argument below constructs the homotopy directly instead.

proof.text: Let $q:\coprod_{n,a\in K_n}|\Delta^n|\to|K|$ be the defining quotient map of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Its product with $[0,1]$ pulls $\widetilde h$ back to the continuous prism maps just constructed, one on each disjoint summand. The interval is locally compact: every relative neighborhood of $t$ contains $[\max(0,t-\epsilon),\min(1,t+\epsilon)]$ as a compact relative neighborhood for sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$. Apply [lem-cbc-quotient-cylinder-continuity] with $X_0=\coprod_{n,a}|\Delta^n|$, $X=|K|$, $T=[0,1]$, and $Z=|L|$. It gives continuity of $\widetilde h$ for the ordinary product topology, with no compactness or Kan condition on $K,L$. At $t=0$ use $R_n$: the final level-$1$ weight is zero, so the endpoint is $|h_0|$. At $t=1$ use $R_0$: the initial level-$0$ weight is zero, so the endpoint is $|h_1|$.

source.place: Construction 3.6.5.1 (0148), for a 1-simplex in Fun(K,L); explicit agent prism expansion of the continuous realization homotopy. Corollary 3.6.2.2 (013E) supplies the source's finite-factor product identification; the argument below constructs the homotopy directly instead.

proof.text: Apply this construction to $H$ and $J$. For any simplicial map $f:K\to L$, its realization is $[a,\lambda]\mapsto[f(a),\lambda]$: it is continuous by the quotient definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and respects the relations because $f$ is simplicial. This same formula proves $|vu|=|v|\circ|u|$, $|uv|=|u|\circ|v|$, and $|\mathrm{id}|=\mathrm{id}$. Thus the two constructed continuous homotopies have endpoints $|v|\circ|u|,\mathrm{id}_{|A|}$ and $|u|\circ|v|,\mathrm{id}_{|B|}$. If one is in the opposite order, precompose its interval coordinate with the continuous function $t\mapsto1-t$. The two orders can be adjusted independently. Hence $|u|$ and $|v|$ are two-sided continuous homotopy inverses.

source.place: Construction 3.6.5.1 (0148), for a 1-simplex in Fun(K,L); explicit agent prism expansion of the continuous realization homotopy. Corollary 3.6.2.2 (013E) supplies the source's finite-factor product identification; the argument below constructs the homotopy directly instead.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak] with $X=|A|$, $Y=|B|$, $f=|u|$, $g=|v|$ and the homotopies just oriented from the composites to the identities. Its hypotheses are continuous maps and two continuous homotopies for ordinary product topologies, all supplied in Steps 4 and 5. It gives a bijection on path components and a group isomorphism $\pi_n(|A|,x)\to\pi_n(|B|,|u|(x))$ for every $n\geq1$ and every $x\in|A|$, even though the homotopies need not fix basepoints. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] these are exactly the weak homotopy equivalence conditions for $u$. If either simplicial set is empty, existence of both $u$ and $v$ forces both to be empty; the component map is then the empty bijection and there are no source basepoints. The construction and conclusion also apply in this case.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_homotopy_equivalence_weak {A B : SSet.{u}} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ A) (H : A ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ A) (J : B ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ B) (hH : (SSet.ι₀ ≫ H = f ≫ g ∧ SSet.ι₁ ≫ H = 𝟙 A) ∨ (SSet.ι₀ ≫ H = 𝟙 A ∧ SSet.ι₁ ≫ H = f ≫ g)) (hJ : (SSet.ι₀ ≫ J = g ≫ f ∧ SSet.ι₁ ≫ J = 𝟙 B) ∨ (SSet.ι₀ ≫ J = 𝟙 B ∧ SSet.ι₁ ≫ J = g ≫ f)) : IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence f
